_note: The COST analog of complexity-budget.json — set at project START and guard it as the design grows, with `python tools/cost/check_cost.py --game games/<slug>` and the bg-architect agent. Fewer UNIQUE component TYPES is the biggest lever (each type = its own tooling/assembly/QC), then box size (drives freight + tariff exposure), then piece count. A game that busts its cost budget has two honest outcomes: cut/merge components back under, or consciously (and log-ably) accept a higher price tier / thinner margin. `target_cogs_fraction` is the manufactured unit cost as a fraction of retail (indie POD ~0.5; a healthy pitch/crowdfund target is ~0.2). `unit_cost_per_type` are ROUGH at-volume order-of-magnitude figures (USD, pre-freight, pre-tariff) — re-verify with a live manufacturer quote before pricing. Tighten for a small-box filler; loosen for a bigger boxed game. See knowledge/cost-and-manufacturability.md.
